title: Close the HumbleStudio professional baseline and release gate
summary: Prove that internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace meets its declared professional, performance, accessibility, data-safety, agent, and assurance baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Reconcile all open and proposed foundation, professionalization, and assurance tickets against current main.
Close or explicitly defer broken functionality, data-safety, privacy, security, warning, and test-trust gaps before claiming baseline completion.
Run the strongest practical static, build, unit, integration, migration, accessibility, localization, and runtime gates appropriate to the repository.
End with zero app-owned warnings; suppressions and threshold increases require narrow reviewed exceptions with expiry.
Record representative performance baselines and adopt repository-owned budgets for critical journeys and resource risks.
Verify loading, empty, error, offline, stale, permission-denied, interruption, and recovery behavior for the primary product surfaces.
Verify persistence, export/import, backup/restore, migration, or idempotence boundaries where the product owns durable state.
Define privacy, credential, logging, diagnostic, retention, deletion, and support-bundle boundaries.
Verify accessibility and localization through behavior and runtime evidence, not only source inspection.
Publish a current verification plan and coverage graph for critical invariants.
Classify remaining gaps by risk and distinguish unavailable evidence from failure.
Add an independent or adversarial review proportionate to the highest remaining risk.
Capture the closest practical runtime proof: browser, device, hardware, filesystem fixture, local process, or distributed build as applicable.
Verify monetization-specific invariants only when the declared model `internal-now-optional-commercialization-later` requires them.
Publish the repository agent/runtime profile and prove that undeclared tools or permissions are rejected.
Refresh release, rollback, support, and external-service posture without performing release actions.
Ensure status, tickets, documentation, evidence, and code tell the same story.
Record every gate not run and why.
Define a regression-sentinel or repeatable re-verification command for each critical invariant.
Mark the professional baseline complete only when current evidence supports the claim.

blocked_by.reason: The capstone scope depends on reviewed earlier-wave foundations.
blocked_by.unblock_condition: The following tickets are solved or equivalent evidence exists: HS-0068, HS-0064, HS-0066

trigger.source_ref: Jan requested Wave 10 as the largest and most thorough final planning wave across the entire portfolio.

agent_notes: Portfolio Capstone and Operating System Wave 10.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, merge products, mutate external data, delete, restore, or enable monetization from this planning ticket.
Alternative considered and rejected: adding more disconnected ambitious features without charter, capacity, assurance, and product evidence would make the portfolio less trustworthy.
Wave 10 is a realization and rationalization layer, not a reason to keep expanding the backlog indefinitely.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `required-prerequisite`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-charter-input`, relevance `next`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `use as governing context, not another parallel backlog`. Portfolio and product charters remain decision inputs, while Wave 11 and Wave 12 own implementation and completion.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-product-charter-input` / `next` / priority `high`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid`; publication `publish-after-fresh-reconciliation`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.
